documents.title: Follow-up: PHN, DM
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Neurology dx postherpetic neuralgia in Dec, started gabapentin, now at 300 TID since mid-Dec. Pain "half what it was," sleeping better. A little woozy the first week, gone now. No falls.
Neurology said we can manage refills here if stable -- happy to.
Meds: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, latanoprost OU qHS, gabapentin 300 TID, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.
O: BP fine. Right T5 band still tender to touch, healed skin. Gait steady.
A/P:
1. PHN -- improving on gabapentin. Continue; refills from us. Kidney function normal so dose is fine.
2. T2DM -- A1c today.
3. Shingrix: now's a good time; first dose at a nurse visit, second 2-6 mo later.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP -- 06/10/2024
Ms. Klein returns with progressive osteoarthritis. We saw her for her hands in 2021, and orthopedics saw her right knee in 2022 and 2023. Knees ache and stiffen after standing or walking for a while; rest helps, the day makes it worse. She has noticed bony swellings developing on her fingers.
Meds: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, latanoprost, gabapentin 300 TID (for post-shingles pain), acetaminophen. NKDA. Smoker, 35 pack-years.

Exam: right knee tender along the medial joint line; Heberden nodes at the DIP joints; no warmth, erythema or swelling of any joint. Right side worse than left.
Procedure: a small-volume aspirate was obtained from the right knee under sterile technique to exclude an inflammatory or crystal process. Synovial fluid: white cell count 420 cells/uL, no crystals -- noninflammatory.

Assessment: Generalized (nodal) osteoarthritis -- hands and knees, R knee most symptomatic. No inflammatory arthritis.
Plan: continue acetaminophen, strengthening and weight management. Return as needed.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit and Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV + chronic care visit. 69F, here with her daughter.

Daughter's concerns (pt present, agrees "a little"): over roughly the last 10 months mom has been more forgetful -- misplacing her keys and glasses, repeating questions on the phone, mixed up the January appointment week. Still managing her own pills with the alarm box; daughter checks the box on Sundays now. Pt feels it's normal aging; her own mother had Alzheimer's late in life and she's worried about that.
No falls, no head injury, no new meds since gabapentin in late 2023. Mood fine -- PHQ-2 0. No alcohol.

Chronic problems: HTN, T2DM, HLD, obesity, tobacco use (1 ppd, ~39 pack-years), POAG (ophtho, stable), nodal OA hands/knees, PHN on gabapentin.
Meds: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, latanoprost OU qHS, gabapentin 300 TID, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, pleasant, conversant, a bit hesitant on dates. Neuro: no focal deficits, gait normal. Heart/lungs normal. Feet normal.

A/P:
1. Memory concerns, ~10 months, family history. Reversible causes: TSH and B12 with today's labs. Gabapentin can dull thinking -- she's on a modest dose and it's controlling the pain, so leave for now. Referral to geriatric psychiatry memory clinic for a full evaluation (wait is long, ~6 months). Daughter to help with appointments and medications.
2. T2DM / HTN / HLD -- labs today; no changes.
3. Tobacco -- counseled again. LDCT due -- ordered.
4. PHN -- stable on gabapentin, refills here.
F/u 6 months, or after the memory evaluation.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Dorothy (and Karen-on-copy if Dorothy shares this): labs from Tuesday are good. Thyroid normal, B12 normal -- so nothing simple there to explain the memory changes, which is why the memory clinic visit matters. A1c a little above 7, fine for you with no change. Kidneys fine, cholesterol at goal. The memory clinic will call to schedule; let us know if you don't hear in 3 weeks.

documents.title: Geriatric Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
GERIATRIC PSYCHIATRY -- MEMORY CLINIC CONSULTATION, 12/01/2025
Referred by PCP for memory evaluation.

Ms. Klein is a 69-year-old woman accompanied by her daughter, who reports a year and a half of steadily worsening forgetfulness and confusion. She misplaces everyday items around the house, has lost her way driving on roads she knows well, and at times cannot find the word she wants. Her daughter also notes she is more irritable than she used to be, with some change in personality.
History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, open-angle glaucoma, osteoarthritis, postherpetic neuralgia. Current smoker, 35 pack-years; no alcohol. Mother with late-onset Alzheimer disease.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg, latanoprost OU, gabapentin 300 mg TID, acetaminophen. NKDA.

Exam: oriented to person only -- not to place or date. Neurologic exam without focal findings. MMSE 22/30.
MRI brain (11/20/2025): diffuse cortical atrophy, greatest in the hippocampi and temporal lobes.
Prior labs from PCP (TSH, B12) normal.

Impression: Alzheimer disease.
Plan:
- Donepezil 5 mg at bedtime; increase to 10 mg after 4 weeks if tolerated. Possible nausea, vivid dreams, slow pulse.
- Daughter to supervise medications.
- Follow up 6 weeks.
cc: PCP

documents.title: Mom's memory clinic visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Karen, Dorothy's daughter, writing from her account. The memory doctor said it is Alzheimer's and started her on donepezil. Did you get their letter? I'm taking over her pills. Should she still be on everything else?

documents.title: RE: Mom's memory clinic visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Karen, yes, the letter and MRI report arrived last week and the doctor has them. Keep her other medications as they are for now. Please call the front desk to book a follow-up visit with the doctor so we can go over everything together -- she's overdue for her diabetes check as well.

Pulse 72, regular.
Plan: continue donepezil 10 mg nightly. Return in 3 months.
cc: PCP
